solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Temporary visit curtailed around America westwards

indicators.note: around says the shortened visit word is wrapped about the other piece
curtailed means docked of its tail, so the last letter goes

parts.note: to call on someone is to visit them

indicators.note: in an across clue, going westwards means reading right to left

parts.note: USA is the United States of America

explanation.surface: A short trip that gets cut short somewhere in the United States, heading west.
explanation.walkthrough: 'curtailed' docks the last letter of the visit word, and 'westwards' runs America backwards, as across entries read right to left; 'around' wraps one round the other.
explanation.definitionFit: Casual work or staff is temporary, taken on occasionally rather than permanently.

clue.text: Animal bone found underneath roughly half-hour later

parts.note: CA, short for circa, means roughly or approximately
a rib is a bone of the chest

indicators.note: half of the word hour here is its central pair of letters, the two ends dropped

explanation.surface: A bone discovered beneath something about thirty minutes afterwards.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'found underneath' and 'later' only set the order of the pieces; 'half' of hour is its middle two letters.
explanation.definitionFit: The caribou is the North American reindeer, a large wild animal of the deer family.

clue.text: Caught, one's inclined inside to confess using defunct money

indicators.note: inside says the caught-and-hill pieces go within the confessing word

parts.note: to sing is slang for confessing to the police
C is the cricket abbreviation for caught
a hill is something inclined, a slope

explanation.surface: Someone caught out feels moved to own up while spending old cash.
explanation.walkthrough: CHILL goes after the S of SING. The schilling was Austria's currency before the euro.
explanation.definitionFit: The schilling was the Austrian currency unit, replaced by the euro, so it is money no longer in use.

clue.text: Insist upon having a nap in auditorium

indicators.note: an auditorium is where an audience listens, so this signals a word heard rather than read

parts.note: in racing tips a nap is the day's best bet, a cert (a certainty)

explanation.surface: Someone demands the right to doze off during a performance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Nap' looks like a snooze, but it is the tipster's term for a horse thought sure to win: 'a cert'. 'in auditorium' signals the sound.
explanation.definitionFit: To assert a claim or right is to insist upon it firmly.

clue.text: Correct gear used by hospital during stroke

indicators.note: during says the gear and hospital pieces come in the middle of the stroke

parts.note: a putt is a stroke in golf
rig means equipment or gear

explanation.surface: Fixing equipment a hospital uses while a patient has a stroke.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Stroke' suggests a medical emergency beside 'hospital', but it is a golf stroke.
explanation.definitionFit: To correct an error is to set it straight, a verb phrase of the same sense.

clue.text: Rising bowler, perhaps second in Australian state

indicators.note: second in picks the second letter of the word Australian
rising in a down clue means the word is read from bottom to top

parts.note: a bowler is an example of a hat

explanation.surface: An up-and-coming bowler, maybe the second-best in an Australian state side.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bowler' sounds like cricket next to 'Australian', but it is the hat, and 'Rising' turns it upward. Utah is a US state, not an Australian one.
explanation.definitionFit: Utah is one of the fifty states of the USA, home to Salt Lake City.

clue.text: Mexican farmer managed business while nursing that lady

parts.note: ran means managed, as in ran a shop

indicators.note: nursing means holding close, so the business abbreviation holds the lady pronoun

parts.note: CO is short for company, a business
her refers to that lady

explanation.surface: Someone ran a business while caring for a particular woman.
explanation.definitionFit: A ranchero is a rancher or farm worker in Mexico and the American Southwest.

clue.text: Canines seen in centrepiece of voguish fashion brand

indicators.note: seen in says the two letters sit inside the other piece
centrepiece of takes the central letters of the word voguish

parts.note: C stands for canine in dental notation, so two canines are two Cs

explanation.surface: Dogs spotted at the heart of a stylish label's display.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Canines' are not dogs but teeth, written C in dental notation; 'centrepiece of' takes the middle three letters of voguish.
explanation.definitionFit: Gucci is a famous Italian luxury fashion house.

clue.text: One rambles on in outskirts of Thirsk with king and queen

indicators.note: in says the on-word sits between the outer letters
outskirts of picks the first and last letters of Thirsk

parts.note: re means on or about, as in a letter heading
K is the chess abbreviation for king
ER is Elizabeth Regina, the Queen

explanation.surface: A walker goes on and on around the edge of a Yorkshire market town with royalty.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rambles on' suggests chatter, but 'on' is a piece of the wordplay. Thirsk is a market town in North Yorkshire.
explanation.definitionFit: A trekker is a hiker making a long walk, someone who rambles across country.

clue.text: Deposit's placed by that woman going back for change

indicators.note: placed by says one piece sits beside the other
going back in an across clue means the word reads from right to left

parts.note: her refers to that woman
ash is the deposit left after burning

explanation.surface: A woman returns to the bank to swap a deposit for cash.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Deposit' suggests a bank, but it is the residue a fire leaves.
explanation.definitionFit: To rehash is to rework old material with little real change, so the verb means alter or rework.

clue.text: Pub clean after shifting sticky thing?

parts.note: a bar is a pub

indicators.note: shifting says the letters of clean are moved about

explanation.surface: Tidying a pub after the shift ends, and finding something gummy.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags that 'sticky thing' is a playful description rather than a dictionary one.
explanation.definitionFit: A barnacle clings fast to rocks and hulls, so it is a thing that sticks.

clue.text: Postpone article about entertainer associated with us

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the article goes round the other pieces

parts.note: an is the indefinite article
a DJ, disc jockey, entertains a crowd
our means associated with us, belonging to us

explanation.surface: Delay a story about a performer linked with our group.
explanation.walkthrough: 'associated with us' defines the possessive, belonging to us.
explanation.definitionFit: To adjourn a meeting is to suspend it until a later time, putting it off.

clue.text: The Spanish invade second-rate city?

indicators.note: invade means go into, so the Spanish article enters the other word

parts.note: B-grade means second-rate
el is Spanish for the

explanation.surface: Spanish forces invade some lesser city.
explanation.definitionFit: Belgrade is the capital of Serbia, a city on the Danube.

clue.text: Personnel probe error with £1,000 contract

indicators.note: probe means poke into, so the personnel pair goes into the error word

parts.note: a sin is an error or wrongdoing
HR, human resources, is the personnel department
K stands for a thousand, as in a 50K salary

explanation.surface: The personnel department investigates a mistake in a thousand-pound deal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'contract' looks like a noun for a deal, but it is the verb; the psychiatrist sense of the answer is a red herring beside 'probe'.
explanation.definitionFit: To shrink is to become smaller, the same as to contract.

clue.text: Bolt, a month back, ripped off

parts.note: to bolt is to flee

indicators.note: back means the month abbreviation is reversed

parts.note: Dec is short for December

explanation.surface: Someone who bolted a month ago was swindled.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bolt' looks like a noun for a fastening, but it is the verb, run away; 'back' turns DEC into CED.
explanation.definitionFit: To be fleeced is to be cheated or overcharged, robbed of money.

clue.text: Building block not in use, partly being restored

indicators.note: restored, as in going back, means the taken letters are read in reverse
partly means only some of the letters of these words are taken

explanation.surface: A building block lying idle is partly under restoration.
explanation.walkthrough: 'partly' takes TINU from 'not in use', and 'being restored' reverses it.
explanation.definitionFit: A unit is a single standard component from which larger things are assembled.

clue.text: Standard celebration — I'm taking a spin in limousine

parts.note: a jolly is a party or outing

indicators.note: in says the turned word sits within the car abbreviation

parts.note: RR, Rolls-Royce, is a luxury limousine

indicators.note: taking a spin means the word is turned round, read backwards

parts.note: ego is Latin for I, the self

explanation.surface: A party where I go for a ride in a luxury car.
explanation.walkthrough: 'taking a spin' sounds like a drive but reverses EGO to OGE, set inside RR. 'Standard' means a flag.
explanation.definitionFit: A standard is a flag, and this is the skull-and-crossbones flag flown by pirates.

clue.text: Plum contract acquired by faceless monster

indicators.note: acquired by says the monster piece takes hold of the next one
faceless means without its front letter

parts.note: an ogre is a monster
to engage someone is to contract them for work

explanation.surface: A lucrative contract snapped up by a monster with no face.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Plum' looks like an adjective for a juicy job beside 'contract', but it is the fruit. 'faceless' turns OGRE into GRE.
explanation.definitionFit: A greengage is a green variety of plum.

clue.text: Perhaps bitter about work after key cut

indicators.note: after says the ale piece follows the key

parts.note: Esc is the escape key on a keyboard

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the ale wraps the work

parts.note: bitter is an example of ale
op, short for opus, is a work

explanation.surface: Maybe a bitter drink about a job after a key reduction.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cut' is a cut of meat, not a reduction.
explanation.definitionFit: An escalope is a thin slice of meat, a cut beaten flat.

clue.text: One heartless soul in there redesigned shopping centre?

indicators.note: redesigned means the letters are rearranged into a new layout

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one

indicators.note: heartless means the middle letter is removed

parts.note: a ghost is a soul or spirit

explanation.surface: A ghost town of a shopping centre redesigned around a lone heartless spirit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'heartless' cuts GHOST to GHST; 'redesigned' rearranges I, GHST and THERE.
explanation.definitionFit: The high street is a town's main shopping road, a shopping centre in the loose sense.

clue.text: Aspiring fliers, with head for heights, enter the new chopper

indicators.note: enter says the cadets and initial go inside the rearranged word
new means the letters of the are made afresh, rearranged

parts.note: the ATC, Air Training Corps, is a UK cadet group for would-be airmen

indicators.note: head for picks the first letter of heights

explanation.surface: Would-be pilots with a head for heights board the new helicopter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'new' rearranges the to HET, and the cadets plus initial enter after its first letter. 'chopper' looks like a helicopter but is an axe.
explanation.definitionFit: A hatchet is a small axe, something used for chopping.

clue.text: Fibre to edge front of pullover

parts.note: a hem is a sewn edge

indicators.note: front of picks the first letter of pullover

explanation.surface: Wool to finish off the front of a jumper.
explanation.definitionFit: Hemp is a plant fibre used for rope and coarse cloth.

clue.text: When one in chess game accepts signal to stop?

indicators.note: accepts means takes in, so the chess piece holds the stop signal

parts.note: a pawn is one of the pieces in chess
red is the traffic signal to stop

explanation.surface: A chess question: at what point does a player agree to a call to halt?
explanation.definitionFit: Predawn names a time, the period just before daybreak, answering the question of when.

clue.text: He painted scores at cricket match around stand

indicators.note: around says the cricket scores wrap the other word

parts.note: runs are the scores made in cricket
to be is to stand or remain, as in let it stand, let it be

explanation.surface: An artist tallies cricket scores around the grandstand.
explanation.walkthrough: 'stand' looks like a grandstand at the ground, but it is the verb, BE.
explanation.definitionFit: Peter Paul Rubens was the Flemish Baroque painter.

clue.text: Almost all fruit attracts Charlie's pet?

indicators.note: attracts means draws in, so the cut fruit takes in the letter
almost all means the last letter is dropped

parts.note: the tomato is botanically a fruit
Charlie is the radio alphabet word for C

explanation.surface: Nearly all the fruit is drawn to Charlie's pet.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Almost all' cuts TOMATO to TOMAT, and C goes inside.
explanation.definitionFit: A tomcat is a male cat, a common household pet.

clue.text: Country woman hides voice

indicators.note: hides means conceals within, so the woman wraps the voice

parts.note: ma is a mother, a woman
alt is an old word for a high voice, alto

explanation.surface: A rural woman keeps her voice hidden.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Country' looks like an adjective for a rural woman, but it is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Malta is an island nation in the Mediterranean.

clue.text: Speeches regularly claim monarch wasting energy with succession

indicators.note: claim means take in, so the alternate letters hold the queen piece
regularly picks every other letter of speeches
wasting means losing, so the energy letter is taken out

parts.note: a queen is a monarch
E is the physics symbol for energy

explanation.surface: Speeches regularly claim that a queen squanders energy on her succession.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wasting' drops just one of the monarch's two Es.
explanation.definitionFit: A sequence is a series of things following one another in order.

clue.text: Relish, most common in pizzas, is from Provence

parts.note: Z is the letter that occurs most often in pizzas, twice
est is French for is, Provence being in France

explanation.surface: A relish, found in most pizzas, comes from Provence.
explanation.definitionFit: Zest means relish or keen enjoyment.

clue.text: Oscar got married, following passage that's sacred

indicators.note: following says the pieces Oscar and got married come after the passage word

parts.note: a hall is a passage or corridor
Oscar is the radio alphabet word for O
wed means got married

explanation.surface: Oscar married in a holy corridor.
explanation.walkthrough: 'following' just puts HALL in front.
explanation.definitionFit: Hallowed means made holy, consecrated.

clue.text: Greek character wrong to raid mother's local booze

indicators.note: to raid means to burst into, so the letters enter the mother word

parts.note: ma is a mother
eta is a letter of the Greek alphabet
X is the mark for a wrong answer

explanation.surface: A Greek character wrongly raids his mother's pub for drink.
explanation.walkthrough: 'local' looks like a pub, but here it means Greek: the drink belongs to Greece, where the clue's character comes from.
explanation.definitionFit: Metaxa is a Greek brandy, a spirit native to the country of the Greek character.

clue.text: Burlesque party held by Turks Head, a filthy place

indicators.note: held by says the party sits between the other letters
head means the first letter of Turks

parts.note: a sty is a pigsty, a filthy place
a rave is a party

explanation.surface: A comic party at the Turk's Head pub turns out to be in a dump.
explanation.walkthrough: The Turk's Head is a common British pub name.
explanation.definitionFit: A travesty is a grotesque parody, much as a burlesque mocks by exaggeration.

clue.text: Having scratched head, Earnest shows injury at the back

indicators.note: injury suggests damage, so the remaining letters are knocked about
scratched head means the first letter is struck off

explanation.surface: Earnest, scratching his head, displays a wound behind.
explanation.walkthrough: Dropping the E gives ARNEST, which 'shows injury' rearranges.
explanation.definitionFit: Astern is a nautical term for at or toward the rear of a ship.
